subject: URGENT: NimbusPay production spike after model v4.2 + mixed-precision profile
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena@nimbuspay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production spike: p99 latency + hallucination increase after v4.2-qdeploy

Sean —

We pushed your v4.2 model upgrade (customer-perf profile + mixed-precision v2.1) last night at 02:30 UTC and started seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency (~900ms -> 2.8s) and a spike in hallucination reports from our fraud-detection candidates. Throughput (req/s) is down ~18%. Attached is a small sample of the error traces and a few example responses that look wrong.

This is customer-impacting: several merchants are reporting timeouts and we’re getting paged. Please advise next steps and whether you can roll us back to v4.1. We need an ETA for mitigation — if you prefer a short call we can do that.

— Elena
Senior Platform Lead, NimbusPay
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: p99 latency + hallucination increase after v4.2-qdeploy

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I’m sorry you’re seeing this.

We’ve queued an incident triage and are pulling perf traces right now. I’m copying our infra and account teams. Preliminary ask: can you confirm the percent of traffic that was routed to the new quant profile (mixed-precision v2.1) vs a fallback? Also, if you can leave the deployment in place we’ll pull live KV cache samples — but we can roll back immediately on your confirmation.

Irene and Ben — can you join the war room? I’ll get a short exec status once we have a plan.

Short call? I’m available at :50 past the hour for a 20m sync.

— Sean
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production spike: p99 latency + hallucination increase after v4.2-qdeploy

Team — initial triage notes (attached perf-traces-20280829.zip):
- Observed tail latency increase correlating with model shard cache misses and higher KV lookup times after mixed-precision (FP16/INT8) kernel path engaged.
- Memory pressure on hosts that run the mixed-precision kernels is higher, causing more frequent GC in the per-request telemetry collector (adds ~200–400ms when it fires).
- A subset of requests that hit the INT8 path show token truncation edge cases that can manifest as answer corruption (likely quantization underflow for rare tokens).

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Rollback to v4.1 (safe, fastest; requires routing change — we can push within 10–15m).
2) Toggle customers onto the fallback pure-FP16 profile (we can flip at the routing layer if Nimbus wants to keep v4.2 for other customers).
3) Apply emergency per-host kernel config to force less aggressive packing (mitigating memory pressure) — higher latency risk for some requests, needs 30–45m.

I recommend option 1 for customer-facing SLA risk. I’ll prepare a rollback playbook (attaching rollback-playbook-aug29.md).

— Irene
VP, Serving Reliability
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rodriguez <elena@nimbuspay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: customer-facing impact & commercial ask

Looping legal/AMs for a quick alignment. Quick points for the record:
- NimbusPay is in a committed Reserved plan (Q3 commit) and this is a customer-impacting outage.
- They have asked about rollback and asked for an ETA for mitigation.
- They’ve indicated potential merchant chargebacks if timeouts persist; we should be explicit about credits and next steps.

Laura — can you advise on standard commercial remediation for a partial outage? I’ll draft a proposed 30% credit for the window we observe (subject to CTO sign-off).

Also, Rishi — once you confirm the rollback mechanics, please add the PB status to JIRA RED-3318. We need to keep Nimbus PM updated (they’re on standby).

— Ben
Head of Sales — East
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Production spike: p99 latency + hallucination increase after v4.2-qdeploy

Action plan and status:
- Confirmed root cause: interaction between mixed-precision kernel selection and tokenization edge paths that hit INT8 encode for rare UTF-8 tokens; plus memory packing triggered on the heaviest shards. Evidence: packet traces + token decode mismatches in nimbus-error-sample-aug29.txt.
- Immediate action: rolling back routing for NimbusPay to v4.1 and the established FP16 profile. Rollback window = now -> expected complete 15 minutes after routing change.
- Post-rollback: we will run a canary of v4.2 with a mitigated kernel config (reduced packing aggressiveness) against internal traffic + synthetic prompt set. If the canary is clean for 6 hours we’ll reintroduce with a controlled ramp.
- Longer-term: add token-level quantization tests to our model onboarding CI and expand the decoding regression suite to include rare unicode scenarios.

I’m executing the rollback now and will update JIRA RED-3318 with timestamps.

— Rishi
Head of Serving Platform
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@nimbuspay.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun@payments-ops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: p99 latency + hallucination increase after v4.2-qdeploy — rollback complete

Elena / Arjun —

Rollback to v4.1 + FP16 profile completed at 17:56 PDT. Early telemetry shows p99 back under 950ms and throughput returned to expected baselines; we’ll continue monitoring for the next 24 hours and share a summary report.

Next steps we committed to:
- Postmortem within 48 hours including timeline, root cause analysis, and compensating actions.
- A limited canary of v4.2 with safer kernel packing scheduled for tomorrow at 10:00 PDT against internal traffic only.
- Commercial: Ben/Laura will follow up on the proposed credit and SLA remediation; I’ve added the relevant HubSpot note HS-523401.

Irene and Rishi — thanks for the rapid turnaround. I’ll set a short exec sync at 09:30 tomorrow to brief the leadership team (CTO & Head of Sales will be present).

— Sean
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
